sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the command

sections.name: main
sections.title: Main lint run
sections.what: Walks through the Python files in the services and packages folders, runs both rule checks on each, prints every problem, and returns a pass or fail result.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single pass over the codebase gives one complete list of problems. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The skip rule for the tests folder is easy to get wrong, so changes to folder names need the rule updated too.

sections.name: entry point
sections.title: Command start point

sections.why: Likely reason: lets the file be run as a command as well as imported. Reason not stated in the code.

summary: Runs every rule check over the project's services and packages folders and prints each problem found.
purpose: Gives the developer one command that reports every rule break before code is accepted.
why: Likely reason: one entry point runs all checks so none are forgotten. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Starts from the current folder, reads each Python file under the services and packages folders, skips virtual environment files and the lint package's own tests, runs the ownership and share checks on each file, prints every problem to the error output with its file and line, and returns a failing code if any were found.
inputs: Python source files under the services and packages folders of the current working folder.
outputs: Printed lines naming each problem's file, line, code and message. The exit code is 1 when any problem is found, otherwise 0.
risks: A file that is not valid Python stops the whole run with an error rather than being reported. The skip test compares the last three path parts, so it only excludes that exact tests folder.
debug: Run the command from the repository root, since the folders are looked up from the current folder. If a file is missed, check the skip rule. If the run crashes, check whether the failing file has a syntax error.
